subject: Success Blueprint + Eval Slate for OrbitSoft — starter draft
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orbitsoft.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orbitsoft.com
Date: 2027-05-10T15:22:00Z
Subject: Kickoff: Success blueprint + evaluation timeline

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. OrbitSoft's engineering and data teams were impressed with the latency and cost numbers you shared. We're trying to move quickly and would appreciate a lightweight mutual action plan (success blueprint) and an initial evaluation slate so we can align internal stakeholders here.

Specifically, can you share: 1) a template MAP we can co-edit, 2) a one-slide close runway showing milestones and decision points, and 3) a suggested 30–45 day eval cadence (key tests, owners, and acceptance criteria)?

We also need to loop in procurement — I copied them on this note. Tentatively looking at a pilot kickoff the week of 5/17 if that works for your team.

Appreciate it —
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Data Platforms, OrbitSoft
liam.oconnor@orbitsoft.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Date: 2027-05-10T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Success blueprint + evaluation timeline

Liam —

Great to hear — glad the demo resonated. I've attached a starter Success Blueprint (Google Doc) and a short Close Runway slide deck. Both are intentionally lightweight so we can iterate in the doc with your stakeholders. Quick notes below and proposed next steps: 

Attachments (shared):
- redwood_success_blueprint_v1.gdoc — MAP template with sections: objectives, success metrics, stakeholders, milestones, blockers, test suite, and sign-off criteria.
- close_runway_timeline_v1.gslides — 2-slide summary: 30/60 day milestones + decision gates.

Proposed next steps:
1) I can open editing to OrbitSoft — if procurement prefers view-only until contract terms are aligned, let me know.
2) Quick sync: Wed 5/12 10:00am PT or Thu 5/13 2:00pm PT — 30 minutes to align owners and the pilot kickoff date.
3) We'll nominate owners for the eval tests (we typically recommend eng lead + CS engineer + security reviewer).

If that works, I'll loop in Marcus (sales) and Monica (CS) to align on pricing guardrails and success criteria.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T09:13:00Z
Subject: OrbitSoft MAP — internal alignment / who owns what

Team —

Looping you in on OrbitSoft (deal OS-4721). Liam asked for a lightweight MAP + slide runway; I shared the starter assets and proposed Wed/Thu syncs. Key asks I want us to cover before the external call: 

- Pricing guardrails: Marcus, can you draft two pilot pricing options (1-week pilot + 30-day pilot) and a recommended SLA/credit language for the pilot? Keep options simple (consumption vs. capped pilot).
- Success criteria & tests: Monica, please sketch 3 acceptance tests we can run during the pilot (latency under X ms at p95, throughput scenario, quality eval against their prompt set). Include owner for each test.
- Security checklist: Aditya, can you pull the minimum evidence items procurement typically asks for (SOC2, data retention, VPC details) and a note on what our Private deployment vs Hosted options would imply?

I've left comments in the doc (redwood_success_blueprint_v1) with suggested owners. We should be ready to present those on the sync. I put a couple of possible blockers in the doc (VPC window, procurement timeline).

Marcus — if you can have the pricing options by EOD 5/11 that gives me time to include them in the slide before the external sync. Monica — a draft of the three tests by 5/12 morning would be ideal. Aditya — a short checklist by 5/12 would be great.

Thanks —
Irene
